summary: Iteration 12 (AI-engine toggle + BYOK error-attribution bug fix, FULL STACK, REELS_MOCK=0) — 5/5 backend pytest cases PASS against the public preview URL and the frontend Settings toggle works as designed (tap-to-switch, correct notes, backend PUT confirmed). BACKEND: (1) PUT /api/settings {key_mode:'builtin'} persists; GET returns key_mode='builtin' and has_own_key=false; (2) unknown/empty key_mode values are correctly coerced to 'own' (server.py:1634 ternary handles this); (3) in 'builtin' mode a saved BYOK key is IGNORED for generation (user_keys() returns ('','') — server.py:383-385) BUT is still REPORTED to the client (openai_key_set=true + masked value preserved so the user can flip back without losing their key); (4) with an INVALID own OpenAI key + key_mode='own', POST /api/script returns 402 with a detail that NAMES OpenAI as the user's key, says 'was rejected', offers switching to 'Built-in credits', and does NOT tell the user to 'top up your Universal Key' — verified by regex on the detail string (classify_error → OwnKeyError branch, server.py:456-471); (5) switching the same throwaway account to key_mode='builtin' successfully reroutes POST /api/script to the Universal key (returned 200 with a real 15s script) — proves the toggle actually changes generation-time key selection. Each throwaway account was DELETEd via /api/auth/me at the end of each test class. Admin's real keys were never touched. FRONTEND (Settings, /settings): logged in as admin (russngina@gmail.com), tapped settings-button, saw the AI engine segmented control with testIDs key-mode-own + key-mode-builtin. Initial state renders 'My own keys' active with the red 'AI Image reels need BOTH keys: OpenAI (script & voice) and Google/Gemini (images)...' note. Tapping key-mode-builtin instantly switched the highlight and rendered the blue note 'Using the app's built-in (Universal) credits. Your saved keys are kept but ignored until you switch back.' — as required. The PUT /api/settings {key_mode:'builtin'} fires and the DB does persist the change (verified by direct authenticated GET). Tapping key-mode-own switched back and re-rendered the red 'AI Image reels need BOTH keys' note. Navigating away (back button) and re-entering Settings preserved the last-selected mode (own note remained visible). BOTH testIDs (key-mode-own, key-mode-builtin) are present, tappable, and correctly wired to setKeyMode() (settings.tsx:147-162).

integration_issues.issue: On a hard reload of /settings, api.getSettings() runs in useEffect (settings.tsx:81-86) BEFORE the auth token is attached to the api client, so the first GET /api/settings returns 401 (visible in browser console). The catch swallows the error and settings state stays null, so the UI falls back to the default `settings?.key_mode ?? 'own'` and re-renders the 'own' segment + red 'AI Image reels need BOTH keys' note EVEN THOUGH the DB has key_mode='builtin'. Backend persistence is 100% correct — verified by direct authenticated GET /api/settings after the reload (returned 'builtin'). The UI state self-heals on the next in-app navigation to Settings, but on cold reload the user sees the wrong toggle position and the wrong info note. Same class of auth-hydration race documented in iteration_11 for /series/[id]. Fix: gate the useEffect fetches on user hydration (e.g. `if (!user) return;` in the effect, with user in the deps), or retry the GET once auth flips from null → present.

react_native_issues.issue: Pre-existing React 19 warning `props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents` — appears on virtually every screen (settings, auth, home). Not new in this iteration.
Pre-existing warning `[expo-notifications] Listening to push token changes is not yet fully supported on web` — web-preview limitation only.

action_items: OPTIONAL POLISH (recommended): In /app/frontend/app/settings.tsx useEffect at line 81-86, gate the initial api.getSettings() / api.getConfig() calls on the auth user being hydrated (add `user` to the effect deps and early-return when !user), or on a 401 from getSettings retry once after refreshAuth(). Currently the first fetch after a hard reload races the auth token and returns 401 → settings state stays null → the UI falsely renders the 'own' segment even when the DB has key_mode='builtin'. Backend is fine; this is purely a client-side hydration order bug.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:380-385 (user_keys) — Correctly returns ('','') when key_mode=='builtin', so generation code paths receive the empty-key sentinel and fall back to the Emergent Universal key. Simple, clean, no leakage of the user's saved key when they've opted out. Good.

server.py:388-403 (public_user) — has_own_key correctly = bool(oa or gk) AND mode=='own' (so it flips to false in builtin mode even when a key is saved), while openai_key_set / google_key_set / *_masked continue to reflect what's stored (so the UI can still show 'Yours · sk-...' and offer to switch back). Exactly the right split.

server.py:452-471 (classify_error) — The OwnKeyError branch attributes 401/403/'invalid api key'/'unauthorized' to the user's own provider name ('OpenAI' or 'Google / Gemini') and points them at platform.openai.com / aistudio.google.com AND offers 'switch AI engine to Built-in credits'. Quota/billing/429 also correctly attributed. The fallback (line 472+) still uses the 'Universal Key' language ONLY when it's the shared key that actually failed — that's the right split. Verified by regex on the 402 response: 'openai' present, 'top up your universal' absent, 'built-in' present.

server.py:1633-1634 — `upd['key_mode'] = 'builtin' if req.key_mode == 'builtin' else 'own'` — correctly coerces any non-'builtin' value (including empty string, 'garbage', 'invalid') to 'own'. Confirmed by test_invalid_key_mode_coerced_to_own.

pipeline.py (OwnKeyError wrapping) — assumed correct because test_bad_own_openai_key_blames_openai_not_universal passes; the /script endpoint clearly receives an OwnKeyError with provider='openai' when the user's saved key fails, not a generic exception.

settings.tsx:147-162 (setKeyMode) — Optimistic update (setSettings before the PUT), await api.updateSettings({key_mode}), reconcile from response, refreshAuth(), toast on success, rollback via getSettings() on failure. Well-designed. Only nit: no debounce/loading state on the segmented control (user can double-tap and fire two PUTs). Not a bug — the server is idempotent.

settings.tsx:81-86 useEffect — DOES NOT wait for auth user hydration before fetching /settings. On a cold reload this fires before the api client has attached the token, GET /api/settings returns 401, the catch swallows it, and the toggle renders the 'own' fallback state EVEN WHEN the DB has 'builtin'. See integration_issues[0]. Fix: `useEffect(() => { if (!user) return; ... }, [user])`.

settings.tsx:222 Section hint text (line 222) still says 'Leave blank to keep using built-in credits.' — that sentence is now slightly misleading because leaving a key blank in 'builtin' mode is a no-op (the key is already ignored). Minor copy nit — could tweak to 'Leave blank OR flip AI engine → Built-in credits to use built-in.' Not blocking.

settings.tsx:227-242 — Both segments are Pressable with distinct testIDs (key-mode-own, key-mode-builtin), correct active-state styling driven by `settings?.key_mode`, and the icon+text combo satisfies the 44pt touch-target guideline. Good.

settings.tsx:244-255 — The blue 'built-in' note and the red 'own' note are mutually exclusive on `settings?.key_mode`, and both are correctly wrapped in <Text> inside <View>. No raw-text-in-View issues.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The AI-engine toggle + error attribution feature is fully wired backend-side. Regression file: /app/backend/tests/test_keymode_toggle.py. Frontend testIDs: key-mode-own, key-mode-builtin (both under settings-button). The known cold-reload race on /settings is a UX-only cosmetic (backend persistence works — verify with a direct authenticated GET /api/settings if in doubt). Auth: register field is `access_token` (not `token`). Login endpoint is /api/auth/login (JSON body {email,password}) — same as /api/auth/register. Admin bypasses BYOK/subscription gate; throwaway free-tier users can still call /api/script because /script only checks moderate+quota (not BYOK-gated, unlike /reels/batch/scripts). When testing error attribution, keep key_mode='own' explicitly (the default) to trigger the OwnKeyError branch; if you PUT key_mode='builtin' the saved bad key is ignored and /script hits the Universal key which succeeds.
rca_of_issue: Original bug: 'out of AI credits / top up Universal Key' when the user's OWN OpenAI/Google key errored. Root cause: pipeline exceptions raised while calling the user's own key were reaching classify_error() as plain exceptions, so the budget/429/quota regex on line 478 wrongly matched and returned the Universal-Key top-up message. Fix (already implemented): pipeline now wraps user-key failures in `pipeline.OwnKeyError(provider=..., original=...)`, and classify_error's isinstance() branch on line 456 attributes those to the correct provider ('OpenAI' or 'Google / Gemini') and points the user at their own provider dashboard, offering a switch to 'Built-in credits'. Added feature (already implemented): key_mode field on user document ('own'|'builtin') with default 'own', PUT /api/settings accepts key_mode, user_keys() returns empty tuple in 'builtin' mode to force the shared Emergent key path, and Settings screen exposes the choice via a segmented control (key-mode-own / key-mode-builtin). Confirmed both fixes work end-to-end. The only remaining ergonomics gap is the cold-reload UI flicker documented above.
